title: fix(sync): confirm each retirement candidate against GitHub instead of vetoing the whole repo
description:
Closes #54.

## The problem

`sync --full` retires mirrored issues GitHub no longer lists, so a transferred issue's source row doesn't linger as a ghost. (Ghosts are harmful: the row freezes at `state='OPEN'` forever and pairs with its own transferred copy at cosine ~1.0, so dedup proposes closing the **live** issue as a duplicate of one that no longer exists.)

To avoid deleting live data, that came with a whole-repo veto: if GitHub reported more issues than the walk saw, retire nothing. **That veto misfires on exactly the repos it matters for.** The walk pages `UPDATED_AT DESC`, so an issue commented on mid-walk jumps to an already-visited page and is absent from the walk while being perfectly alive. `rstudio/shiny` is ~56 pages of issues over minutes of wall time — a single comment in that window trips it. Reconciliation would rarely, perhaps never, run there.

It was also blind to the failure it was written for: a **partially truncated** response leaves the walk's count self-consistent with a smaller repo, so the comparison passes and everything past the truncation point is deleted.

## The fix

Absence from the walk now only makes an issue a *candidate*. `confirm_retirable` then asks GitHub about that one issue, and the row is deleted only on a confident answer:

| Response | Verdict | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `gone` | retire |
| 200, repository differs from the one queried | `transferred` | retire, logging the destination |
| 200, repository matches | `live` | **keep** — the walk simply missed it |
| read failed | `unknown` | **keep** — a rate limit is not absence |

This is strictly stronger than the count comparison: every deletion is now justified by a direct statement from GitHub about that specific issue, which also closes the truncation hole (truncated pages yield candidates that are still live, and each is individually refused).

## Verified against live GitHub, not assumed

The premise — that a confirmation read distinguishes a *transferred* issue from a *deleted* one — was checked before being built on. Transferred issues leave gaps in the source repo's numbering, so I enumerated `rstudio/thematic` (158 numbers present, max 165 → 7 gaps) and probed each:

- `thematic#145` → 200 → `rstudio/shiny#3902`. Corroborated independently: that issue's timeline carries a `TRANSFERRED_EVENT` naming `rstudio/thematic`.
- `thematic#44` → 200 → `rstudio/bslib#83`.
- `thematic#133`–`#137` → 404.

## Cost

Reads scale with candidates, not repo size, and candidates are normally zero. `thematic` has 7 gaps across ~15 years, so a full sync there spends ~7 extra requests. For scale: the active 4-repo pilot is a ~30-request full sync; the full 41-repo fleet ~767.

## Circuit breakers retained

Two whole-repo refusals remain, both about the walk rather than the issues:

- **Empty response** — the walk saw nothing while the mirror holds rows.
- **Implausible candidate share** — more than `RETIRE_MAX_SHARE` (10%) of mirrored issues missing at once, which also avoids spending a read per candidate to reject hundreds one at a time.

⚠️ **A judgement call worth reviewing:** a strict 10% cap makes retirement impossible on small repos (2 mirrored rows → 10% is 0.2, so any single retirement exceeds it). So there's a `RETIRE_MIN_ALLOWANCE = 5` floor. The effective allowance is `max(5, 10% of mirrored rows)`. The floor wasn't in the original spec discussion — flagging it explicitly rather than burying it.

`totalCount` stays in the query and the log as diagnostic context explaining *why* candidates exist, but is no longer a veto.

## A test-hygiene fix that fell out of this

An autouse fixture now fails any test in this module that reaches the real `gh` transport. It immediately caught **several pre-existing tests silently depending on the network** — passing only because the fake repo `r/a` 404s, which reads as "gone". They were asserting a confirmed deletion while confirming nothing. All now inject a fake confirmer.

## Verification

`make check` (validate-yaml, compile-scripts, py-check, js-check) passes: **451 tests**, up from 437. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-reconcile-confirmation-read-design.md`.

## Follow-up

#57 covers persisting the `old -> new` mapping the redirect reveals, so a transferred issue isn't re-analyzed from scratch in its new home and the review app's Transfers worklist can resolve itself. Deliberately out of scope here — this PR uses the destination only to justify a retirement and make the log legible.

title: feat: implement cross_repo_option — link-duplicate, suggest-transfer, and mirror reconciliation
description:
## What and why

The dedup stage has always asked the model, for duplicate pairs spanning two repositories, for a `cross_repo_option` of `close-and-link` / `keep-both-link` / `transfer`. That value was computed, stored in `dedup_verdicts`, displayed to reviewers — and **never acted on**. Every cross-repo duplicate got identical treatment.

This gives the field meaning. `proposals.build` now maps each value to a **distinct action**, so an action name always describes what approving it does:

| `cross_repo_option` | action | executor plans |
|---|---|---|
| `close-and-link`, or `null` | `close-duplicate` | comment + close `not planned` — **unchanged** |
| `keep-both-link` | `link-duplicate` | comment linking the sibling, **no close** |
| `transfer` | `suggest-transfer` | adds `wrong location`; **a human moves the issue** |

Same-repo pairs are untouched — still GitHub's native duplicate close.

**The system gains no ability to transfer an issue.** `src/triage_verse/gh.py` is byte-identical to `main`, `transferIssue` appears nowhere in `src/`, and neither new action is in `autonomy.ELIGIBLE` or `executor.AUTO_ELIGIBLE`. Tests assert all of that, including that the guard's wire-field backstop refuses `transferIssue` even when smuggled under an allow-listed operation name.

## Root cause of the dead field

The three option names appeared in **no prompt, rubric, or taxonomy** — the only other occurrence of "transfer" in the repo was the rubric line forbidding auto-transfer. The model was picking from an undefined enum, so the stored values were noise. Defining them in the dedup prompt was the prerequisite, not polish.

## The UI is the feature

Because the executor never transfers, approving a `suggest-transfer` only applies a label — and approved proposals leave the queue. Without somewhere to land, every approved suggestion would vanish with nobody having moved anything. So there's a **Transfers** tab: a worklist of suggestions whose label has actually been applied, each with its destination and a *Mark transferred* control.

## A prerequisite bug this exposed

Making `transfer` actionable made an existing latent bug reachable. When an issue is transferred, GitHub gives it a new number in the target repo and it leaves the source. Sync is upsert-only, so the source row froze at `state='OPEN'` **forever**. That ghost then paired with its own transferred copy — byte-identical title and body, cosine ~1.0 against a 0.80 threshold — and dedup would propose **closing the live issue as a duplicate of one that no longer exists**, or transferring it back.

Full syncs now diff the mirrored set against GitHub and delete what vanished (row, comments, and embedding — the row must go, because `embed_repo` has no state filter and would otherwise re-create the vector). Two guards prevent deleting live data: reconciliation refuses when GitHub reports more issues than the walk saw, and refuses outright when a repo returns zero issues while the mirror holds rows.

Reconciliation runs on **full syncs only** — an incremental walk stops at its cursor, so absence there means nothing.

## Review notes

- `decisions/2026-07-27-absent-from-mirror-is-not-reviewable.md` records that this **reverses a documented decision** in the Plan 3 review-queue design ("absence isn't evidence the issue is closed"). The old spec is untouched, per the house rule that specs are immutable.
- `undo` now reverses both new actions. It previously could not — `_reverse_mutations` dispatches on *action*, not mutation *kind* — and worse, reported success while doing nothing and poisoned the record so a corrected undo would skip it.
- Rebased onto main after #40 landed; `record_transferred` takes `decided_by` and the app supplies `current_actor()`, attributing the confirming actor rather than whoever approved.

## Known limitations, deliberately not fixed here

- On a busy repo the `totalCount` guard may **chronically refuse**, since any issue commented on mid-walk trips it. Direction is fail-safe (deletes nothing, logs loudly) but ghost cleanup may rarely fire on the largest repos. A targeted re-check of only the missing candidates is the fix.
- An approved `suggest-transfer` whose execution never happens or errors appears in neither the queue nor the Transfers panel.
- Coverage is limited to issues dedup paired **across repositories**. A plainly misfiled issue that duplicates nothing gets no suggestion — that needs a per-issue classification signal and a separate design.

## Verification

`make check` (validate-yaml, compile-scripts, py-check, js-check) passes: **437 tests**, ruff and pyright clean.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-transfer-suggestion-design.md` · Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-cross-repo-option.md`

title: feat: record decided_by + reason on review decisions (#40)
description:
Closes #40

## Summary
Every human review decision now records **who** decided (`decided_by`) and, on reject/edit, **why** (`reason`), so the append-only decision log is audit-ready as the program adds reviewers and autonomy. `decisions.record()` gains a required `decided_by` keyword and an optional `reason` (written only when non-empty; no migration — readers already use `dict.get`). A cached `decisions.current_actor()` resolves the reviewer identity via `gh api user` → `$USER` → `"unknown"` (never raises; passes the egress guard as a REST read). The review app stamps the actor on all three human paths (`on_decide`, `approve_visible`, `app_audit_reject`), captures an optional reason via a modal on every reject, and seeds the edit modal's reason from the agent's proposal rationale. Automated `execute --auto` is intentionally unchanged (`decided_by="autonomy"`), so `autonomy.py`'s `!= "autonomy"` precision filter is unaffected.

Live verification surfaced two Shiny module-namespacing bugs, fixed here: opening a modal from a Queue row (a Shiny module) namespaced the modal input ids, so the top-level save handler never fired. Task 4 regressed the row **Reject** button this way (silent no-op); the row **Edit** button had the same latent bug pre-existing. Both now route through a shared `_module_modal_relay(opener)` factory that builds the modal in the top-level session. Keyboard/drawer paths were already top-level and unchanged.

## Verification
- `make py-check` — ruff format+lint, pyright (0 errors), 356 tests pass.
- Live review app (seeded mirror + proposals, driven in a browser): approve writes `decided_by` with no `reason`; reject (row + drawer) writes `rejected` + `decided_by` + optional `reason`; edit (row) opens with `reason` seeded from the rationale and writes `edited` with edited `params`, original `proposed_params`, and `reason`. Inspected `.data/decisions/*.jsonl` each time.

title: feat(db): retain decision history via append-only classifications and dedup verdicts (#20)
description:
Closes #20

## Summary
Converts the two decision tables (`classifications`, `dedup_verdicts`) from current-state upserts to append-only history so the live mirror is the complete record — no more archiving old DB snapshots to answer "what did triage decide last run." Each table's primary key is widened with `run_id`, so every analyze run writes a new history row. Within a single run the `recheck` stage still refines that run's row (`store()` keeps `ON CONFLICT … UPDATE` on the widened key), giving **one row per run** rather than per store. Two new views (`classifications_latest`, `dedup_verdicts_latest`) return the newest row per key; current-verdict read paths (`db.get_classification`, `db.get_dedup_verdict`, and `tier1`'s "fixed" detection) now read the views, so behavior is unchanged. `proposals.build()` intentionally stays on the base tables filtered by `run_id` — it builds from the run just completed, which is already exactly one row per key. Existing databases are migrated in place by a `PRAGMA user_version`-gated rebuild in `db.connect()` that preserves current rows as the first history entry per key. Spec and plan live under `docs/superpowers/`.

## Verification
`make py-check` (ruff + pyright + 359 pytest) passes. New coverage: append-across-runs, recheck-within-run (one row), latest-view reads, full-history query, migration (preserve + idempotent + fresh-DB), and tier1 latest-signal. To see history: run `analyze` twice over an issue whose content changed, then `SELECT run_id, model, priority, at FROM classifications WHERE repo=? AND number=? ORDER BY at` returns both verdicts while `classifications_latest` returns only the newest.

title: feat(analyze): halt on claude_cli rate limits instead of burning retries
description:
Closes #24

## Summary
Under the #19 worker pool, several concurrent `claude -p` calls hit Claude Code's subscription rate limits at once. Previously every failure — including a rate limit — counted against `submit_one`'s 2-attempt content-quality retry budget, wasting both attempts (and their spend) on a load-driven condition. This PR detects rate-limit failures and halts the analyze stage breaker-style instead.

Research confirmed `claude -p` already does its own exponential backoff (up to 10 retries) on transient 429/529, so any rate limit reaching us is a *sustained* one where in-run sleeping is pointless — hence halt-and-resume rather than back-off-and-retry (full rationale and rejected alternatives in `docs/superpowers/specs`).

Key pieces: `_default_runner` now surfaces the CLI's JSON error envelope on a non-zero exit (it was previously discarded); `_is_rate_limit` detects 429/529 via `api_error_status` or a defensive `result`-string match (not the version-varying `subtype`); `submit_one` returns a new `rate_limited` status on the first hit without burning an attempt; `analyze` halts both the sequential and parallel submission paths (`halted_on_rate_limit` plus `_is_halted`/`_apply_halt` helpers), draining in-flight workers and metering their spend, leaving the item to re-queue via the content-hash cache. The `anthropic_batch` backend and the content-quality retry budget for non-rate-limit errors are untouched.

## Verification
`make py-check` passes (351 tests, ruff + pyright clean). New tests cover: `_default_runner` returns stdout on a non-zero exit (and still raises when stdout is empty); `_is_rate_limit` across status codes, usage-limit strings, and negatives; `submit_one` returning `rate_limited` with a single runner call while a generic error still burns both attempts; and sequential + parallel stage halts that re-queue the affected item and set `halted_on_rate_limit`.

title: fix: re-queue orphaned synchronous batch on restart instead of KeyError (#25)
description:
Closes #25

## Summary

The `claude_cli` backend (`ClaudeCliClient`) keeps batch results only in memory (`self._batches`). If a process is killed after `analyze._submit_stage` commits a `submitted` batches row but before that row is collected, the row survives while the results it points at die with the process. On restart, `analyze`'s resume logic adopts the surviving row and calls `client.results(provider_batch_id)`, which raised `KeyError` on the fresh instance. This was a pre-existing narrow crash-window bug (present since `184a486`), not introduced by the worker pool.

This adds an explicit reconciliation step. `ClaudeCliClient`/`FakeBatchClient` gain a `recognizes(provider_id)` predicate (true only for ids this instance submitted). At the top of `analyze()` — before the stage-started gates — `_reconcile_orphaned_sync_batches()` drops any `submitted` batch a synchronous client no longer recognizes and re-queues its items via the existing `clf_hash`/`get_classification` caching. It is a no-op for async backends and any client without `recognizes`. `db.delete_batch()` removes the batch row and its items.

## Verification

`make py-check` passes (ruff, pyright, 341 tests). Two new tests drive the fix: `test_recognizes_only_provider_ids_this_instance_submitted` (unit) and `test_orphaned_synchronous_batch_is_requeued_after_restart` (seeds a surviving orphaned `submitted` row and asserts `analyze()` no longer raises, drops the row, and re-classifies the issue).

title: feat: credential egress guard for GitHub writes (#41)
description:
Closes #41.

## What & why

Routes **every credentialed GitHub write** through a single fail-closed choke point in `gh.py`, so a misfired prompt, a bug, or a compromised dependency can't use the `gh` token against the wrong repo, endpoint, or verb. The blast radius of "the prompt misfired" becomes a logged refusal, not an incident.

## Design (decided during brainstorming)

- **One transport.** All issue-mutating writes are unified onto **GraphQL** via a single helper `gh.gh_mutation(operation, query, variables, *, repos)`. Porcelain (`gh issue edit/close/reopen`) and REST-write shapes are gone from the codebase's write paths.
- **Guard in `run_gh` (fail-closed classifier).** Every call is classified before `gh` launches:
  - **Safe reads** (REST GET, GraphQL queries, `repo view`) → allowed.
  - **Trusted infra** (`release view/list/download/create/upload/delete` for the state-bus snapshots on the hub repo; explicit `--repo` redirection refused) → allowed.
  - **GraphQL mutations** must pass **three** checks: an **operation-name** allowlist (our policy unit), a **wire-field** allowlist parsed from the query string (fail-closed backstop against a lying declaration), and a **declared-repo** check against `config/repos.yaml` (canonicalized — the kata pagination lesson).
  - **Everything else** → refused with `EgressRefused` (a `GhError` subclass, not retried).
- **Repo scoping.** GraphQL has no repo in the URL, so the write path *declares* its target repos and the guard checks them against `repos.yaml`. Bounded by the single choke point + the mutation-field allowlist.
- **Operation names vs GraphQL fields.** `addLabelsToIssue`/`removeLabelsFromIssue` are our names (issue/PR granular); they compile to GitHub's shared `addLabelsToLabelable`/`removeLabelsFromLabelable` fields. `addLabelsToPR`/`removeLabelsFromPR` reserved for later.

## Migrations

- `executor.py` — all writes (`add/remove-label`, `comment`, `close`, `close-duplicate`, `reopen`, undo `delete-comment`) rewritten to guarded GraphQL; node IDs resolved via REST reads.
- `tier2.py` / `reprex.py` — label-adds moved to a shared `gh.add_issue_label` on the guarded path.
- `snapshot.py` `release` ops recognized as trusted infra (no code change).

## Tests

- New `test_gh_guard.py`: classifier per-shape (allow/refuse), mutation-field parser (aliased-injection catch), repo check + canonicalization, bypass guard (raw porcelain write refused before subprocess), and an **end-to-end test that runs the real executor query constants through the actual classifier**.
- `FakeGh` rewritten to model GraphQL mutations as real state; executor/tier2/reprex tests assert resulting state, not call shapes.
- Full suite **312 passing**; `make check` green (pytest + node + pyright + ruff + yaml).

## Docs

Spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-egress-guard-design.md`), plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-egress-guard.md`), and a `CLAUDE.md` architecture note documenting the choke point.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(cli): global --json output mode on every command (#42)
description:
Resolves #42.

Adds a global `--json` flag to the `triage-verse` CLI so every command emits a single, machine-readable JSON envelope on stdout — for scripts, dashboards, and coding agents driving the CLI without screen-scraping prose.

## What it does

- **`--json` in either position:** `triage-verse --json sync` ≡ `triage-verse sync --json`, including nested subcommands (`analytics export --json`).
- **Uniform envelope:** every command emits one JSON object:
  - success → `{"command": <str>, "ok": true, "exit_code": <int>, "data": <obj|array>}`
  - failure → `{"command": <str>, "ok": false, "exit_code": <int>, "error": <str>}`
- **`ok` means "did the command run to completion?"** A negative-but-successful result (a `verify-counts` mismatch, an `execute` with errors) is `ok: true` with a non-zero `exit_code`; only bad input and unexpected exceptions are `ok: false`.
- **Logs move to stderr** in JSON mode so stdout carries only the envelope. The codebase's logging-visibility convention (stage markers, heartbeats) is preserved, not suppressed.
- **All ~16 subcommands** covered: sync, verify-counts, analyze, analyze-status, embed, execute, undo, analytics export, snapshot publish/bootstrap, state pull/push, tier1, tier2, autonomy status, steady-state.
- **Human mode is unchanged** — non-`--json` output is byte-for-byte the same.

## How

A small `Output` helper in `cli.py` centralizes routing (`log`/`emit`/`fail`); the flag is wired via a shared `argparse` parent parser (`SUPPRESS`-defaulted) plus a top-level definition, and `main()` wraps dispatch so exceptions become `ok:false` envelopes under `--json`. `analytics.export()` now returns its payload so JSON mode can emit it.

## Docs

- Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-cli-json-output-design.md`
- Implementation plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-cli-json-output.md`
- README gains a "Machine-readable output (`--json`)" section.

## Testing

`make check` green — 290 pytest + 43 node tests, ruff format/lint + pyright clean. New `tests/triage_verse/test_cli_json.py` exercises the envelope shape, both flag positions, stderr log routing, domain-negative exit codes, and error envelopes. Live smoke test confirmed real commands emit a single valid JSON object on stdout with logs on stderr.

🤖 Built via spec → plan → subagent-driven TDD execution, with a final whole-branch review that caught and fixed a steady-state stdout log leak.

title: feat: robust review queue — skip invalid-module-id proposals + prune command (#30)
description:
Resolves #30.

## Problem
The review app renders each proposal as a Shiny dynamic module keyed on the proposal `id`. Shiny's `validate_id` only accepts ids matching `^\.?\w+$`; any other id raises `ValueError` at render — and since the whole queue renders in a single `queue_ui` output, **one bad id blanks the entire queue**, not just that row. Latent today (real ids are `uuid4().hex`, always safe), so it only surfaces from a hand-edited proposal record.

## Changes
- **`review_queue`**: new `valid_module_id()`; `load_undecided` now drops proposals whose `id` fails the module-id rule, logging an actionable warning — consistent with the existing malformed-JSON skip, so one bad row degrades gracefully instead of taking down the queue. Filtering at this single funnel keeps rendering, keyboard nav, and stats consistent.
- **New command** `triage-verse proposals prune <id|file> [--apply]` (`proposals.prune_proposals`): removes broken records so the operator can regenerate via `analyze` (GitHub is source of truth).
  - Dry-run by default (`--apply` to rewrite), matching `execute`/`undo`.
  - Only ever removes invalid-id records — passing a valid id refuses and exits non-zero, so it can't delete a good proposal.
  - Rewrites files line-for-line, preserving other lines (blank / malformed) verbatim.
  - Points the operator at `triage-verse analyze` to regenerate.
- The skip warning names the fix: `... Remove it with 'triage-verse proposals prune <id>' ..., then re-run 'triage-verse analyze'.`

## Design
Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-prune-invalid-proposals-design.md`.

## Verification
`make py-check` — ruff + pyright clean, **277 passed** (11 new: unit tests for `prune_proposals`, CLI tests, and `valid_module_id`). Manually smoke-tested the CLI (dry-run / refuse-valid-id / apply).

title: docs: add CLAUDE.md with project conventions (resolve #26)
description:
Resolves #26.

Adds a repo-root `CLAUDE.md` for AI coding agents (and humans) working in this codebase.

## What's in it
- **What the project is** — the `.github/triage/` Actions workflow layer and the `triage-verse` Python CLI.
- **Commands** — `make py-check` as the primary Python gate, `make check` for the full CI suite, `make py-format`, single-test invocations (pytest + `node --test`), and how to launch the Shiny review app.
- **Architecture (big picture)** — the SQLite mirror as derived data, the sync → embed → analyze → review → execute → undo flow, `analyze.py` as a resumable multi-stage state machine with pluggable LLM backend + spend metering, the autonomy/precision graduation loop, and the `triage-state` orphan-branch state bus.
- **Logging-verbosity convention** — captures Barret's standing "lots of logging" preference as a codebase-wide rule: stage start/end markers, heartbeats in wait loops, line-buffered stdout (introduced in `analyze.py`, `a1bf876`).
- **Docs house rules** — purposes of `docs/superpowers/specs/`, `docs/superpowers/plans/`, `decisions/`, and the rule that they're immutable historical records (new record + `Superseded by`, not rewrites). Docs are self-contained with no section-number cross-references.

No code changes; documentation only.

title: feat: review app, executor, and steady-state automation (resolve #9 #10 #11)
description:
Resolves #9, #10, #11 — the human-review surface, the executor, and steady-state automation + escalation tiers. One branch, built serially per Barret's instruction (single PR, not three).

Specs & plans included: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-13-plan-4-executor-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-13-plan-5-automation-design.md` (+ matching plans).

## #9 — Plan 3: Review app
Queue + decisions log, drawer, dashboard, close review, keyboard + edit (shipped across PRs #28/#37/#36/#39/#38). This PR adds to the app: the Tier 2 "Request AI fix" button, the autonomy Audit section, a "Request reprex" button, a **Skipped** tab, and keyboard/safety refinements (see below).

## #10 — Plan 4: Executor (apply approved actions, with undo)
- `triage-verse execute [--apply]` — reads approved/edited decisions → per-issue freshness re-check (`updatedAt` moved → `stale-needs-rereview` bounce, resurfaced in the queue with a badge) → allowlisted mutations via `gh` (label add, priority swap, templated comment + close, close-as-duplicate). **Dry-run by default.** Results ledger written incrementally to `.data/results/`.
- `triage-verse undo --batch <id> [--issue …]` — reverses a batch (labels restored, issues reopened, executor comments deleted); idempotent.
- Comment templates in `config/templates/` (model rationale is never posted).

## #11 — Plan 5: Steady-state automation + escalation tiers
- **State bus:** `triage-verse state pull/push` sync proposals/decisions/results JSONL + `cursors.json` with a `triage-state` branch via exact-line union-merge; mirror snapshots stay on Releases.
- **Steady-state loop:** `triage-verse steady-state` (pull → sync → analyze → tier1 → push → snapshot) and a **dormant** `steady-state.yml` (workflow_dispatch only, cron commented out, `contents:write` — no issue writes).
- **Tier 1** — `triage-verse tier1`: read-only `claude -p` sessions over a cached checkout emit `close (fixed)` proposals into the normal queue; capped/day + spend circuit-breaker. Never mutates GitHub.
- **Tier 2** — `ai-triage:fix-requested` marker label (excluded from `allowed_safe_output_labels`); apply it via `triage-verse tier2 owner/repo#N`, the review-app "Request AI fix" button, or by hand. Dormant, guarded `tier2-fix.yml` (label + weekly-cap guards) opens **draft** PRs only, never auto-merges.
- **Reprex bot** — `ai-triage:needs-reprex` marker label + review-app "Request reprex" button. Dormant, guarded `reprex.yml` runs a read/repro session that **appends** a minimal reprex comment (append-only; never edits existing content) and **never auto-closes**: a non-reproducible issue gets `ai-triage:no-reprex` + `ai-triage:needs-review` and returns to human review.
- **Graduated autonomy** — `triage-verse autonomy status [--write]` computes per-category precision (≥98% over ≥200 reviewed) and writes promotions to `config/autonomy.yaml`; `execute --auto` applies promoted `add-label`/`set-priority` (never closes) above the confidence floor via synthetic `auto-approved` decisions, with a deterministic 10% spot-audit surfaced in the review app.

## Review-app UX & safety (this branch)
- **Skip = "not now":** skipped proposals keep their analysis and move to a dedicated **Skipped** tab (rather than being dropped), where they can be approved/edited/rejected. A skip auto-clears back to the main queue if the issue updates. Only approved/edited/rejected are terminal.
- **Keyboard:** row-button clicks move the highlight; `Enter` toggles the drawer; `↑`/`↓` select; redundant `o` shortcut removed. The drawer is page-level so evidence review works from any tab.
- **Crash guard:** "Request AI fix" / "Request reprex" `gh` calls are wrapped — errors surface as a notification instead of killing the session.

## Safety
CI never mutates issue *content*: the executor is local-only; CI's App-token use is limited to Tier 2 draft PRs and (dormant) reprex comments, which are append-only and never close. Both/all automation workflows ship dormant. Whole-branch reviews on Opus for both plans returned ready-to-merge; the one Important finding (script-injection via workflow inputs) was fixed by routing inputs through `env:` (also applied to `reprex.yml`).

## Testing
`make check` green — 266 Python tests, 43 Node, ruff/pyright/yaml all clean. Built subagent-driven: per-task spec+quality reviews, plus final whole-branch reviews.

title: docs: decision record — keep triage-verse engine, don't adopt kata
description:
## Summary

Adds `decisions/2026-07-10-kata-not-engine.md`, recording the decision to keep triage-verse's own SQLite mirror + pipeline engine rather than adopting kata (katatracker.com) as the internal engine.

Key reasoning captured in the record: kata would replace only the already-built mirror layer — with less data (no PRs), a per-repo polling model that doesn't fit a 42-repo fleet, and v0.9.x maturity risk (we hit a sync-breaking pagination bug, kenn-io/kata#168) — while providing no home for the pipeline state that carries the program's value (embeddings, classifications, dedup verdicts, spend, decisions). The design lessons we did take from kata are tracked as #40 (decision actor attribution), #41 (credential egress guard), and #42 (`--json` CLI output). A hybrid "kata as agent-facing work queue on top" remains open as a future experiment with an explicit revisit trigger.

## Verification

Docs-only change. Read `decisions/2026-07-10-kata-not-engine.md` and check it follows the conventions in `decisions/README.md`: standalone (no section refs into other docs), dated filename, header with Date/Status/Related, options with honest pros and cons, decision with deciding factor, and consequences.

title: feat(review-app): review close / close-duplicate proposals (Plan 3d)
description:
Closes #34 (Plan 3d, child of #9).

## Summary

Extends the review queue to the higher-stakes `close` and `close-duplicate` proposal action types, which the Plan 2 pipeline already emits into the proposals JSONL but `review_queue.SUPPORTED_ACTIONS` filtered out until the evidence drawer (#37) existed.

- `review_queue.SUPPORTED_ACTIONS` now includes `close` / `close-duplicate`; a new `HIGH_STAKES_ACTIONS` frozenset is the single definition the app consults for guardrails. The existing closed-issue filter already drops close proposals whose issue was closed by a human after analysis.
- **Evidence-before-approval guardrail:** close-action rows show a red action badge and only **Review evidence** (opens the drawer) + **Skip** — Approve/Reject for the open proposal live in the drawer's Proposal section, so a close can't be approved from a 280-char snippet. The drawer decide buttons render for every action type and reuse the existing `on_decide` path (same decision records, drawer auto-closes).
- **Bulk approve stays low-stakes:** "Approve visible label/priority rows" (relabeled) approves only non-high-stakes proposals.
- **Duplicate sibling in the drawer** (deferred from Plan 3b): for `close-duplicate`, the drawer renders the sibling issue's title/state/labels/snippet + GitHub link via a new pure `review_queue.duplicate_sibling` helper that derives the sibling from the proposal's evidence URLs (no Plan 2 schema change; existing JSONL records work as-is). `canonical` / `cross_repo_option` params render in words, with `(not stated)` for a null canonical.

Nothing writes to GitHub; approving a close only appends a decision record (executor is Plan 4). Design spec and implementation plan are under `docs/superpowers/`.

## Verification

`make py-check-format`, `make py-check-types`, and `make py-check-tests` all pass (166 tests; new coverage for the widened action set, close-proposal staleness, and `duplicate_sibling` parsing).

Driven end-to-end with a seeded throwaway mirror (one `add-label`, one `close`, one `close-duplicate` pair) via `shiny run` + Playwright: badged close rows expose only Review evidence/Skip; drawer Approve/Reject write correct decision records and remove the row; the close-duplicate drawer shows the sibling's title, state, `bug` label, snippet, and GitHub link; bulk approve decided only the `add-label` row. Repro recipe is in `.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md` (updated in this PR with a proposal-id gotcha found while driving: Shiny module ids reject hyphens).

title: feat(review-app): keyboard-driven review + edit action (Plan 3e)
description:
Closes #35. Part of #9.

## Summary

Adds keyboard-driven review and an edit-before-approve action to the review-queue app, per the design in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-plan-3e-keyboard-review-design.md` (plan in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-09-plan-3e-keyboard-review.md`).

- **Keyboard review:** one queue row is always selected (highlighted, scrolled into view). `j`/`k` move selection, `a`/`r`/`s` approve/reject/skip, `e` edits, `o`/`Enter` opens the drawer, `Esc` closes it. The key→action map lives once in `review_queue.KEY_ACTIONS` and is mirrored into the JS keydown listener via `json.dumps`; keystrokes are ignored while focus is in a form field or a modal is open. Selection clamping (`review_queue.clamp_index`) keeps the highlight on the next row after a verdict shrinks the queue.
- **Edit action** (key `e` + per-row Edit button): a modal pre-filled with the proposal's params. "Approve edited" writes a decision with `verdict: "edited"`, `params` = the corrected value (what the Plan 4 executor should apply, same field as every other verdict), and `proposed_params` = the model's original, preserved for precision analysis.
- **Precision accounting:** `dashboard.category_precision` gains an `edited` column; `judged = approved + rejected + edited` and `precision = approved / judged`, so an edit counts as judged-but-not-approved-as-proposed.

## Verification

`make py-check` passes (162 tests). Driven end-to-end via Playwright against a seeded throwaway `.data/` tree: `j`/`k` move the highlight, `a`/`r` wrote `approved`/`rejected` records and removed rows, decided proposals stayed gone across an app restart, `o` opened the drawer for the selected row and `Esc` closed it, `e` opened the pre-filled modal, typing `a`/`r`/`s`/`e` inside the modal input triggered nothing, and saving wrote `{"verdict": "edited", "params": {"priority": "p1"}, "proposed_params": {"priority": "p3"}}`. The Dashboard precision table shows the new `edited` column with the expected math.

To try it locally: `uv run shiny run src/triage_verse/review_app/app.py`, then review the queue with the keys listed in the legend at the top of the Queue tab.

title: feat(review-app): issue/PR slide-over drawer (Plan 3b)
description:
Closes #32. Part of #9.

## Summary
Adds the GitHub-Projects-style slide-over drawer deferred from the Plan 3a first slice. Clicking a queue row's title now opens a right-hand drawer rendering the full item from the local mirror — title, state (incl. PR merged status), labels, milestone/assignees/reactions, Markdown body, full comment thread, the proposal under review with its linked evidence, and a deep link out to GitHub (`/pull/N` for PRs). Review never requires leaving the app, and nothing is fetched from the network at render time.

Design follows the repo's pure-module pattern: `db.py` gains `get_pr`/`get_comments` read helpers, a new Shiny-free `drawer.py` assembles the drawer payload (`load_item(con, repo, number) -> dict | None`), and `review_app/app.py` stays a thin wire-up — an app-level `drawer_state` reactive value, a `render.ui` panel with ~30 lines of CSS, Close-button and backdrop dismissal, and a "not found in mirror" fallback for deleted/transferred items. The drawer is deliberately one app-level instance so Plan 3c (dashboard) and 3d (dupe pairs) can reuse it by setting the same reactive value. Spec and plan are committed under `docs/superpowers/` (spec chose the plain-Shiny custom panel over `ui.modal` and `shinyreact`; both alternatives documented there).

## Verification
`uv run pytest` (147 tests) covers `drawer.py` and the new db helpers offline. The app itself was driven end-to-end with Playwright against a seeded throwaway `.data/`: drawer opens from a row title with full markdown body + comments (including a "3 comments on GitHub; 2 mirrored" lag note), PR rows show "PR · MERGED" and link to `/pull/202`, a proposal whose issue is missing from the mirror shows the placeholder drawer, Close and backdrop both dismiss, and approving a row writes the decision record and removes the row. Recipe persisted in `.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md`. To try it: seed `.data/` and run `uv run shiny run src/triage_verse/review_app/app.py`, then click any row title.

title: feat: add Dashboard tab to review app (Plan 3c)
description:
Closes #33 (parent #9)

## Summary

Adds the Plan 3c Dashboard tab to the review-queue Shiny app. The existing `analytics.py` series (backlog burndown, opened-vs-closed per week, close-reason mix) are wired into the UI for the first time, with a repo selector switching between all-repos and per-repo views. A new pure module `dashboard.py` computes the remaining metrics from data that already existed: triage coverage (open issues with a classification row, per repo), review throughput (decisions per ISO week), per-category precision (approval rate among judged proposals; skips shown but excluded from the rate), and per-stage spend from the `spend` table. Charts are dependency-free inline SVG generated by a unit-testable string builder — no plotting library added; the two series colors are CVD-validated categorical slots and every chart is paired with a legend and adjacent table. `review_queue._iter_jsonl_records` was promoted to public `iter_jsonl_records` since `dashboard.py` also reads the decisions JSONL tree. The app shell moved from `page_fluid` to `page_navbar` (Queue + Dashboard); queue behavior is unchanged. Design doc: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-plan-3c-dashboard-tab-design.md`.

## Verification

Run `shiny run src/triage_verse/review_app/app.py` with `TRIAGE_VERSE_DB` / `TRIAGE_VERSE_PROPOSALS` / `TRIAGE_VERSE_DECISIONS` pointed at a populated `.data/` tree, open the Dashboard tab, and switch the Repo selector. Verified end-to-end against a seeded 180-issue mirror with proposals, decisions, classifications, and spend rows: all seven metric sections render, the repo filter rescales burndown/flux/close-reasons, approving a queue row updates the queue-depth stat, and an empty `.data/` tree renders "no data" placeholders instead of erroring. `make py-check` passes (ruff, pyright, 150 tests including 12 new in `tests/triage_verse/test_dashboard.py`).

title: feat: add Plan 3a review-queue Shiny app
description:
Closes #31 (Plan 3a; sub-issue of #9)

## Summary
Adds the first slice of the Plan 3 review app (issue #9): a plain Shiny-for-Python queue for `add-label`/`set-priority` proposals, sorted by confidence descending, with per-row Approve/Reject/Skip and a bulk "Approve visible rows" action. New pure modules: `jsonl_log.py` (shared weekly-JSONL append helper, extracted out of `proposals.py` to avoid duplicating it in the new `decisions.py`), `review_queue.py` (loads undecided proposals, filters to in-scope action types and to issues still open in the mirror, sorts by confidence), and `decisions.py` (records verdicts to an append-only log). `src/triage_verse/review_app/app.py` wires these into a standalone Shiny app (`shiny run src/triage_verse/review_app/app.py`, no new CLI subcommand) using Shiny's dynamic-module pattern for per-proposal cards. The `close`/`close-duplicate` proposal types, the issue/PR drawer, and the analytics dashboard are explicitly out of scope for this slice; see the design spec and plan docs added in this PR (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-01-plan-3-review-queue-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-01-plan-3-review-queue.md`).

## Verification
`make py-check` (ruff format/lint, pyright, pytest) — 139 tests passing. Manually verified end to end: seeded fixture proposals plus a mirror issue, ran `shiny run src/triage_verse/review_app/app.py`, and confirmed the queue renders sorted by confidence descending, the mirror snippet and "not found in mirror" fallback both display, Approve/Reject/Skip and bulk-approve all write to `.data/decisions/YYYY/Www.jsonl` and remove the row, decisions persist across a restart, and a proposal whose issue has since been closed in the mirror is excluded from the queue.

title: feat: analysis pipeline (embed, classify, dedup) via claude -p
description:
Closes #8
Closes #19
Closes #21
Closes #23

## Summary

Implements Plan 2 (#8): turns the mirror into triage proposals via local embeddings + duplicate-candidate retrieval + LLM classification/dedup adjudication, driven by a resumable two-wave state machine with spend metering and a `max_usd_per_day` circuit breaker.

Includes a mid-implementation pivot: since we don't yet have an Anthropic Console API key (only Claude Enterprise/Desktop), added a `claude_cli` backend that drives `claude -p` on Claude Code's ambient auth, alongside the originally-designed `anthropic_batch` (Batch API) backend — selectable via `config/models.yaml` `backend:` field. `claude_cli` is the default today; `anthropic_batch` is ready to flip on once a Console key is provisioned (#18).

- Local embeddings (`fastembed` + `sqlite-vec`) for duplicate-candidate retrieval, all issues (open+closed), PRs excluded
- Haiku classification + Sonnet recheck (low-confidence / any close-candidate) + Sonnet dedup adjudication
- `ClaudeCliClient`: schema-validated, retry-once, tools-disabled (`--tools ""`, verified via probe: `num_turns=1`, no real execution) `claude -p` calls; spend from reported `total_cost_usd`; resilient to individual call failures (errored+skip, not crash) with a subprocess timeout
- **Migrated recheck/dedup to Claude Sonnet 5** as soon as it released, with a dedicated decision record (`decisions/2026-07-01-sonnet-5-for-recheck-dedup.md`) documenting a real, measured ~2x per-call cost increase despite equal-or-lower published pricing (likely Sonnet 5's `effort: high` default on Claude Code) — accepted anyway since it only affects the two lowest-volume stages
- Resumable `analyze` state machine (two waves: classify+dedup, then recheck); proposals emitted as local weekly-partitioned JSONL
- Tailable progress logging: per-item `claude -p` call results and stage-level milestones, so a long run can be monitored via `tail -f`
- Prompt-injection containment: untrusted text delimited, schema-constrained enum outputs, no GitHub mutation in this plan
- New CLI commands: `embed`, `analyze`, `analyze-status`
- `decisions/` folder for durable architecture-decision records (fastembed-over-sentence-transformers, Sonnet 5 migration)

**Per-item durability and budget enforcement (issues #21, #23 — fixed):** the `claude_cli` backend chunks at size 1 and persists each item's result to the database immediately after it completes, instead of batching an entire stage (up to 500 items) before writing anything. The `max_usd_per_day` breaker is checked before every item, not once per stage, and a crash mid-run loses at most one in-flight item's spend instead of the whole stage's. Independently reviewed twice (implementation + a dedicated correctness pass); no gaps found.

**Bounded worker pool for concurrent `claude -p` calls (issue #19 — closed):** `config/models.yaml`'s `batch.workers` (default 1, this repo starts at 2) controls how many `claude -p` calls run concurrently via a `ThreadPoolExecutor`. Worker threads only run `submit_one` (no shared state, no DB, no logging); the calling thread owns every database write, the budget check before each new dispatch, and all logging — sidestepping SQLite's single-writer constraint by construction. This widens (but keeps bounded) the same guarantees from #21/#23: overshoot and crash-loss now bound to "at most `workers` items" instead of 1. Reviewed at both the per-task and whole-branch level with high confidence — race-free by construction, halt-and-drain sequence exhaustively simulated, resume semantics confirmed sound (and safer than the pre-existing sequential path). A dedicated parallel-crash-resume test was added and verified non-flaky across 5 reruns.

The non-synchronous (Batch API) path is unaffected by any of the above — same large-chunk async submit/poll/collect flow as before, verified via an unchanged regression test throughout every round of this work.

**Smoke-tested end-to-end, twice**, via `claude -p` (no API key):
- 5-issue slice: `classified=5 rechecked=1`, $0.069 total, proposals JSONL emitted, breaker untripped.
- **Full `rstudio/shinytest2` repo (59 open issues)**: `classified=54 rechecked=8 pairs=0`, **$1.10 total**, 79 proposals written (`set-priority`/`add-label`/`close`), breaker untripped, ran unattended for ~20 minutes (sequential — predates the worker pool). With `workers: 2` now live, a fresh full run would take roughly half that. Dedup adjudication found zero candidate pairs even at full repo scale — plausibly a true negative (no near-duplicate issues in shinytest2) rather than a defect, but its real-call path remains otherwise unexercised. Full results in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-29-plan-2-smoke-notes.md`.

**Follow-up issues:**
- #18 (open) — adopt the Batch API backend once a Console API key is provisioned; the code path is already built and tested, this is a config flip.
- #24 (open, deliberately deferred) — rate-limit-aware backoff for concurrent `claude -p` calls, once real usage shows how the CLI behaves under concurrent load.
- #25 (open, low priority, pre-existing) — a narrow crash window in the sequential `claude_cli` path (a `batches` row surviving a crash between commit and collection) can raise `KeyError` on restart; discovered as an adjacent finding, not introduced or worsened by any work in this PR.
- ~~#21~~, ~~#23~~ (closed) — `max_usd_per_day` and crash-durability now enforced within a stage, not just between stages/runs.
- ~~#19~~ (closed) — concurrent `claude -p` calls via a bounded worker pool.

Design docs: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-29-plan-2-analysis-pipeline-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-29-claude-cli-backend-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-01-claude-cli-worker-pool-design.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `make py-check` clean (ruff format+lint, pyright, pytest) — 125 tests passing
- [x] Every module built via TDD subagents with per-task spec-compliance + quality review, plus whole-branch reviews (pipeline, pivot, the #21/#23 fix, and the worker pool — the latter two independently reviewed on the most capable model given concurrency correctness stakes)
- [x] Real smoke run on shinytest2, 5-issue slice: classification, recheck, spend metering, proposals output all verified
- [x] Real smoke run on shinytest2, full 59-issue repo: same, at scale, unattended, over ~20 minutes, $1.10 total spend
- [x] Concurrency correctness: race-freedom, halt-and-drain termination, and budget-overshoot bounds independently verified by re-derivation and exhaustive simulation, not just by reading the code

title: ci: run PR checks for maintainers with private org membership
description:
## Problem

The `tests` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is **skipped on every `pull_request` event** (even for maintainers), while `push` events to `main` run fine.

The job `if` gate required `author_association` to be `OWNER` or `MEMBER`:

```yaml
contains(fromJSON('["OWNER","MEMBER"]'), github.event.pull_request.author_association)
```

The webhook payload's `author_association` only reflects **public** org membership. A maintainer with **private** membership is reported as `COLLABORATOR`/`CONTRIBUTOR`, so the allowlist silently skips their PR runs.

Verified for `@schloerke`: repo permission `admin`, `public_members` → 404, `members` → 200 (private member).

## Fix

Drop the `author_association` allowlist and rely on the existing same-repo check, which is the real trust boundary:

```yaml
github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
```

A PR branch can only live in this repo if its author has **write access** — outside contributors must fork, which fails this check. Forks and untrusted PRs remain blocked; maintainers are no longer skipped regardless of membership visibility.

Fixes #5

title: feat: shinyverse issue triage program + P1 mirror data plane
description:
Closes #7

## Summary

Establishes the shinyverse issue-triage program and ships **Plan 1 — the P1 mirror data plane**. GitHub stays the source of truth; this adds a local-first hub that mirrors issues into SQLite for analysis. **$0 model spend.**

**Docs**
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-12-shinyverse-issue-triage-design.md` — approved design (local-first hub; rejects GitHub Projects / `gh aw` / `wshm` as the foundation, with rationale)
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-12-triage-verse-p1-mirror.md` — the 12-task P1 plan
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-12-triage-verse-followups.md` — deferred items

**`triage-verse` CLI** (Python, managed with `uv`), driven entirely through the `gh` CLI (no new auth surface):
- **sync** — incremental GitHub→SQLite mirror of issues + PRs + comments (open & closed), cursor-based
- **snapshot** — publish/bootstrap the mirror as GitHub Release assets (`mirror-latest` + dated keep-8)
- **analytics export** — retroactive burndown / weekly-flux / close-reason JSON

**Tooling & CI** — a shinyreact-style `Makefile` whose targets hold every CI command; `ci.yml` runs them via `uv` with the **author-association ownership guard removed** (the same-repo fork boundary is kept); `ruff` + `pyright` gates added. Merged latest `origin/main` (gh-aw triage tooling); Node tests 34 → 43.

Built TDD-style; each task spec-reviewed + quality-reviewed, plus a final whole-implementation review.

## Test plan

- [x] `make check` green — `ruff` (lint + format), `pyright` (0 errors), 58 Python tests, YAML validation, script compile, 43 Node tests
- [x] **Real-data validation on the pilot trio (2026-06-29):**

  - `verify-counts`: **3/3 exact** (reactlog 25=25, shinytest2 59=59, py-shinylive 8=8)

- Known limitation (followups #0): the upsert-only sync leaves stale `OPEN` rows for deleted/transferred issues, so `verify-counts` drifts one direction over time — documented, with a P2 fix path.

title: feat(triage): make gh-aw comparison workflow dry-run only
description:
This PR changes the GitHub Agentic Workflows comparison path to produce a dry-run summary instead of applying labels.

### What changed
- Replaced the label-application safe-output path with a new `summarize_triage_dry_run` flow.
- Added `.github/triage/scripts/dry-run-triage-actions.mjs` to validate proposed triage actions and render a summary without mutating GitHub state.
- Updated the gh-aw output adapter to read the new safe-output tool type.
- Removed the old triage-state persistence script and its test.
- Updated the gh-aw workflow and lockfile so the comparison branch is read-only and uses `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` only.
- Updated the comparison doc to describe the dry-run-only behavior.

### Why
The goal is to compare Claude-based triage with the current repo setup without creating duplicate labels or mutating issues in two parallel workflows. This makes the gh-aw run useful as a side-by-side summary for team review.

### Notes
- The `shiny-triage-gh-aw` branch now stays read-only for GitHub mutations.
- Dry-run output is written to the GitHub Actions summary for easy comparison against the existing workflow.
